title: Crystalline Group-IV Josephson Junction
authors: Frederik H. Knudsen, Axel Leblanc, Patrick J. Strohbeen, Jechiel van Dijk, Yiliu Li, Logan Kusher, Arunav Bordoloi, Alisa Danilenko, Xiangchao Ma, Salva Salmani-Rezaie, Javad Shabani
abstract: Conventional superconducting quantum electronics rely on well-established Josephson junctions made of Al/AlO$_{x}$ where the weak link AlO$_{x}$ is amorphous and is believed to host two-level systems that limit coherence. Crystalline Josephson junctions exhibit atomically ordered interface quality but remain constrained by complex fabrication and intrinsic asymmetry of epitaxial growth. Here, we demonstrate a fully epitaxial approach based on superconductivity in gallium-doped germanium, enabling the realization of Josephson junctions entirely grown in situ by molecular beam epitaxy. These devices feature atomically sharp interfaces and crystalline weak links, resulting in strong Josephson coupling in the ultra-short regime. We observe an unconventional enhancement of the switching current under applied magnetic field, which we attribute to quasiparticle-assisted thermalization processes from the Al contacts. This platform combines structural coherence, fabrication simplicity, and scalability, offering a promising route toward low-disorder, CMOS-compatible superconducting qubits in a merged element transmon architecture.
summary: The paper reports on the creation of novel Josephson junctions using an epitaxial growth technique in gallium-doped germanium. By achieving atomically sharp crystalline weak links, they overcome coherence limitations found in amorphous barriers. The results demonstrate a promising platform for building low-disorder superconducting qubits suitable for integrated quantum circuits.
main_problem: Conventional superconducting quantum electronics are limited by amorphous Josephson junction weak links hosting two-level systems, which degrades qubit coherence.
main_result: The authors demonstrated a fully epitaxial Josephson junction platform using Ga:Ge that maintains structural coherence and shows an unconventional enhancement of the switching current under magnetic field.
method: Electrical transport measurements (I-V curves, dV/dI) were performed on junctions fabricated via MBE to study superconducting coupling in the ultra-short regime.
model_or_system: The system is a Josephson junction formed by crystalline weak links ($	ext{Ga:Ge}/	ext{Si}/	ext{Ga:Ge}$) grown epitaxially. This platform aims to replace amorphous barriers with atomically sharp, crystalline interfaces for superconducting qubits.
key_observables: Supercurrent ($I_{SW}$), differential resistance ($dV/dI$), and the ratio of switching current to retrapping current ($	ext{ISW}/	ext{IR}$) as a function of applied magnetic field ($B$).
important_parameters: The junction operates in the ultra-short regime; key fields include $B^*_{\parallel} = 80 	ext{ mT}$ for $	ext{ISW}$ enhancement.
main_assumptions: The observed magnetic field enhancement of $	ext{ISW}$ is attributed to quasiparticle-assisted thermalization processes from the Al contacts, suggesting an SNS junction character rather than SIS.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows device structure via STEM. Figure 2 compares measured critical current scaling against theory. Figure 3 details the magnetic field dependence of $dV/dI$, showing $	ext{ISW}$ enhancement and hysteresis. Figure 4 examines temperature dependence.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying limitations in existing junctions to presenting the epitaxial Ga:Ge platform, characterizing its structure using STEM, measuring transport properties vs. magnetic field (showing $	ext{ISW}$ enhancement), and finally attributing this behavior to quasiparticle thermalization mechanisms.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses hardware challenges for superconducting qubits by proposing a low-disorder, CMOS-compatible junction architecture, which is central to quantum computing implementation.
